withdrawnRules.RULE_189: WITHDRAWN by ADVISOR ERROR 206, ledger 339.2. It asserted the proposal head is accuracy-bound, not bandwidth-bound. It was built from a table that mixed one student's island-arm ABBA numbers with a ranked receipt from a different prompt population. A cleaner measurement of the same arm with the opposite sign already existed. Every pricing decision that cited RULE 189 is void.
withdrawnRules.RULE_190: Head byte removal returns the predicted cost saving reliably and prompt-independently; the byte model prices it correctly at spec bandwidth (232 GB/s back-solved). All variance lives on the accuracy side and can exceed the cost term in either direction. Never infer bandwidth insensitivity from an arm ordering that changes cost and accuracy together. Only a cell where drafting is bit-identical across arms prices the cost channel.
withdrawnRules.RULE_186_extension: A banked price must carry not only its identity tuple but also whose prompt set produced it.
withdrawnRules.RULE_190_scope: Still stands for the LOCAL byte model. It does not license reading a ranked fraction off a local fraction: the fraction is bytes_removed * steps / (BW * R) and all four terms differ between hosts. That ratio is k, FINDING 331.
withdrawnRules.linear_depth_price_law: REJECTED, RULE 191, ledger 341. R(D) is convex: a quadratic term enters at 27.99 sigma. Never read the zero-draft round off an OLS intercept - it lands below every measured point. Askeladd 43.6 ms = 330.8 GB/s and Edward OLS 50.97 ms = 282.9 GB/s are both above the 273 GB/s M4 Pro spec ceiling and are impossible. Use the MEASURED D=0 point, 65.81 ms = 219.1 GB/s. With it rho over the operating chord 0..7 is 1.387.
withdrawnRules.FINDING_279_at_G2: REFUTED by FINDING 369, ledger 350.7. FINDING 279 predicted about +0.31 % published per extra weight-stream group. The pinned width-5 measurement gives +30.63 % of the round for G = 1 -> 2, that is +28.320 ms/round on a digit-identical accept ledger. Any pricing that cited FINDING 279 at G >= 2 is void.
withdrawnRules.FINDING_348: WITHDRAWN by Edward E164 Q4, ledger 350.6. c47b45be and 24fb4012 are two independent ranked replicates of the same onePass6 arm: spread 1.0972 pp, t = +0.929, p = 0.523. withdrawnRules.delta_s_as_a_cost: RULE 370, ledger 350.5. delta_s = +0.2881 +/- 0.0436 ms/round is an intercept at rows = 0, extrapolated 5.4 rows beyond the observed centroid over a span of [3.30, 7.15] rows. widthSixWall.mechanism: AttentionUtils.swift:104-142 splits a 6-to-9-row causal decode attention into two sdpa calls of at most five rows. The guard is qL * gqa > 32 with gqa = 6, so widths 6 and above fall off the fused sdpa vector path.
widthSixWall.whyItCannotBeRemoved: Above the fused vector path the dispatch changes kernel family and the accumulation order of every score. Widths 6 to 9 then drift from the serial trajectory in top-2 values while ids hold, and the drifted K/V rows contaminate every later round under the ranked exact-value replay. Width 5 measured 5/5 bit-exact.
widthSixWall.closedAlternative: Segmenting the whole forward as two model calls of 5 and k rows was measured bit-exact but pays a second full weight pass of about 25 ms and loses on net. Qwen36MTPBlockSession.swift:1031-1033.
widthSixWall.openQuestion: The split's own comment predicts one extra pass over the KV rows, which prices at 0.4 to 1.3 ms on this host. The measured excess is 14 to 23 ms. The shortfall is a factor of 11 to 18 and that gap is the experiment.

candidateMechanisms.M1: The axis-2 strided slices of cachedKeys and cachedValues materialise full copies. Grows with kL.
candidateMechanisms.M2: concatenated([outA, outB], axis: 2) allocates and copies per layer. Small bytes, so dispatch cost.
candidateMechanisms.M3: Host-side graph build for the extra nodes. Flat in kL.
candidateMechanisms.M4: The excess is not at the sdpa at all.

widthSixWall.candidateFix: Do not slice the cache. Update it twice: append the first five keys and run sdpa A over the returned arrays in full, then append the remainder and run sdpa B over the returned arrays in full, then concatenate. Every window is byte-identical, the kernel family and accumulation order are unchanged, and no slice exists. Removes M1 entirely if M1 is the mechanism.
widthSixWall.fixRisks: The concrete cache class must tolerate two update calls inside one forward, and the second update must not force a reallocation. Check the installed class, not the protocol.
widthSixWall.doesNotContradictPb6: pb6 re-priced width 6 upward and makeBoundaryDepthPrice holds the total constant, so every other step became cheaper. Making the wall physically cheaper changes the cost, not the price.
